query: Our legal team needs to build an automated brief-drafting pipeline. We have a corpus of ~150 case law PDFs and regulatory documents stored at `~/repos/legal-ai/corpus/` that our local RAG system indexes with ChromaDB embeddings. When a user asks a legal question, the system retrieves relevant passages and generates a response with inline citations (e.g., `[Smith v. Jones, 2019, p. 14]`) grounded in the actual source documents. We want to split the workload: keep the vector search and document retrieval local, but then send the retrieved passages along with the user's query to our VPS at `litai.internal:8443` running a newer Claude instance with a larger context window for the actual citation-grounded answer generation. Can you write a Python module `~/repos/legal-ai/src/distributed_drafter.py` that (1) queries ChromaDB locally to pull the top-k relevant chunks with their source metadata (document title, page number, paragraph), (2) constructs a prompt that instructs the remote Claude to produce a legal analysis with precise inline citations referencing only the provided source passages — every factual claim must have a bracketed citation back to a specific document and page, and (3) sends that prompt to the remote Claude endpoint via our existing `send_to_remote_claude()` helper in `~/repos/legal-ai/src/vps_client.py`, parses the response, and validates that every citation tag in the output maps to an actual retrieved chunk before returning the final brief? Include proper error handling for citation mismatches and network failures.

We're launching "GrainRoot," a regenerative agriculture SaaS platform that connects small-scale farmers with direct-to-consumer buyers. Include a tagline, the hero section copy, and the three onboarding emails with subject lines.
